subject: Evergreen VPC connectivity: WireGuard peering & egress proofing
messages:

Subject: Private VPC connectivity for Redwood - quick ask

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're preparing the network-side acceptance checklist for the Redwood private deployment in our PCI environment and want to confirm a few connectivity constraints before we loop procurement. High level asks: 

- Short UX: can Redwood terminate a single WireGuard peer per account in our VPC?
- Egress: we need to prove all outbound connections originate from a small set of nat IPs for egress allowlisting. Can Redwood pin egress controlplane traffic?
- Auditing: do you emit connection-level logs (source/dest/port) and do those integrate with our SIEM?

I've attached a rough diagram from our NetOps team showing the proposed peering hop and an initial policy matrix. Can we do a short architecture review with your network/infra folks tomorrow?

Thanks,
Maria

Director, Cloud Networking
Evergreen Bank

Subject: Re: Private VPC connectivity for Redwood - quick ask

Maria — thanks for the diagram and the clear asks. Happy to run through this. Quick answers up front, then propose a short agenda for the call: 

High level answers: 
- Single WireGuard peer per account: yes, we can terminate a single persistent WireGuard session on the control plane side. For on-prem we recommend a dedicated peer per customer to keep key material scoped.
- Egress pinning: we can ensure control plane egress uses a small pool of NAT IPs per region/tenant. For Dedicated/Private installs we support configurable egress ranges; for Hosted we manage the pool but can provide static NAT ranges for allowlisting.
- Auditing: our control plane emits connection and session logs (timestamp, src_ip, dst_ip, dst_port, session_id) and we can deliver to your S3 or push to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. SOC2 evidence is available on request.

Proposed 30-min agenda for tomorrow:
1) WireGuard handshake and key rotation model (5 min)
2) Egress NAT/pinning and failover semantics (10 min)
3) Control/data plane demarcation and routing (10 min)
4) Logging, retention, and proof-of-delivery (5 min)

Please confirm a time (I have 9–11am PT and 2–4pm PT open). Attaching a draft runbook section with our recommended MTU and keepalive defaults.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private VPC connectivity for Redwood - quick ask

Thanks — adding a few infra notes ahead of the call so we don't go in blind: 

WireGuard termination model (details):
- We terminate WireGuard on the customer-facing gateway in the control plane (Linux userspace + kernel module). Each peer maps to a tenant namespace; keys are rotated on a 30d cadence by default (can be adjusted).
- MTU: recommend 1420 for most enterprise WANs; if you have jumbo-frame segments we can bump but test is required.
- Keepalive: 25s by default to ensure NAT mappings in strict firewall deployments.

Control vs Data plane separation:
- Control plane handles model orchestration, routing decisions, config push, and telemetry collection.
- Data plane (inference nodes) hold the KV caches and serve token-level traffic. For Evergreen we plan a strict egress policy where data plane outbound traffic is only to model artifact registries and internal storage; everything else must traverse the control plane proxy for auditing.

Egress failover: we will provide a small set of standby NAT IPs in the same region; failover is handled via our gateway BGP sessions with the transit provider (if you request BGP) or by switching the NAT pool in the gateway (control-plane triggered).

I'll bring a concise run-through and the endpoint ACLs to the call.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Auditing — retention for connection logs must be 365 days and must be exportable to our SIEM in near real-time (within 5 minutes). Will the runbook capture the delivery SLA?

Also cc'ing my NetOps engineer (netops@evergreenbank.com) who will join the meeting. We're aiming for the call tomorrow at 10:30am PT.

Thanks,
Maria

Follow-up notes from the call (short):

1) BGP peering: we can support static BGP sessions for your transit. Typical parameters: AS preface accepted, MD5 auth supported on quagga/FRR instances. We'll share a template with required ASN ranges and MD5 config snippets.

2) NAT/eIP model: Evergreen will provide two /32 egress IPs per environment (prod/staging). Redwood will route control plane egress through those IPs and emit the egress mapping in logs with session correlation ids.

3) Audit delivery SLA: we will stream connection logs to your HTTPS ingest endpoint and confirm delivery within 3–5 minutes under normal conditions; retention 365d in your S3 bucket is supported (we will set lifecycle per your retention schedule).

4) Runbook action items: finalize MTU test plan, confirm the ASN and MD5 strings, and exchange the WireGuard public keys. I've attached the action-item checklist and a cleaned-up diagram.

Action items (owners):
- Evergreen: provide ASN/MD5 and two egress IPs (netops@evergreenbank.com)
- Redwood (Jonas): share ACLs and a BGP template (by EOD 5/22)
- Redwood (Tessa): send final runbook section and legal intake for procurement if any changes to SLA are required.

Thanks everyone — I'll follow with the attachments.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Network Architect, Redwood Inference
